newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TIGHT SECURITY FOR BURNING ACCUSED
Extra police will be on duty at the Cairns Magistrates Court this morning for the appearance of a man charged over the burning of a six-year-old-boy at a school in the city yesterday.
A 26-year-old Adelaide man has been charged with the attempted murder of the boy, Tjandumurra O'Shane.

He's in the Royal Childrens' Hospital in Brisbane with severe burns after being doused with petrol and set alight yesterday afternoon, while playing with friends in the grounds of the Cairns North State
School.
The school's principal received minor burns to the hands when he and other teachers rushed to the boy's aid.
The boy is the nephew of ATSIC Commissioner Terry O'Shane and New South Wales magistrate Pat O'Shane.
Students at the school will begin counselling today to help them cope with yesteray's trauma, and Education Department officials say help will also be available to school staff.
ASSISTANT TREASURER SHORT REGRETS SHARES MISTAKE
Assistant Treasurer Jim Short says it was a very careless oversight to retain shares in a bank, while being responsible for banking policy.
Senator Short has now sold his 6,000 ANZ shares, after he came close to being sacked by the Prime Minister for breaching the Ministerial code of conduct.
Senator Short says his shareholding did not influence any policy decisions he's made, but he'll donate to charity any profit from the sale of his shares.
He told ABC-TV he regretted placing the Prime Minister in a very difficult position.
Mr Howard says while Senator Short has been careless, he hasn't acted dishonestly.
BURNED BOY HAS ATSIC LINKS
A six-year-old boy burned by an attacker at a Cairns school
yesterday is the nephew of prominent ATSIC Commissioner Terry O'Shane and New South Wales magistrate Pat O'Shane.
Tjandumurra (JAN-da-mar-ah) O'Shane, is in the Royal Childrens Hospital in Brisbane with severe burns, after being doused with petrol and set alight at Cairns North State School yesterday afternoon.
Another of the boy's uncles, Danny O'Shane, says he doesn't believe the attack was racially motivated.
A 26-year-old Adelaide man has been charged with attempted murder and is due to appear in the Cairns Magistrates Court this morning.
The school Principal was treated for burns after trying to help the boy.
TWO WESTERN AUSTRALIAN POLITICIANS QUIT
Two members of the West Austrtalian shadow cabinet have resigned, in the week that the new Labor Party leader, Geoff Gallop, took the helm.
Doctor Gallop formally announced the resignation of controversial MP's John Halden and Norm Marlborough late last night, after urgent talks at Parliament House.
Divisions within the Party emerged this week after details of a Caucus meeting were leaked to the media.
Mr Marlborough has been criticised for his handling of matters relating to Wanneroo Inc, while Mr Halden was under pressure to resign over adverse findings from the Easton Royal Commission.
John Halden also steps down as the Opposition's Leader in the Upper House.
MILITARY EXERCISE KICKS-OFF
A three nation defence exercise involving about seven hundred sailors and a number of air crews will officially kick off in Darwin today.
Lieutenant Jo Bastion says the five day exercise, in waters off the northern coast, will involve personnel from Australia, New Zealand and Singapore.
Lieutenant Bastion says Operation Singaroo aims to strengthen bilateral relationships and enhance cooperation and understanding between the Navies of the the three countries.
AVIATION BOARD NOT RESIGNING
The board of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority is standing firm in the face of Federal Government calls for resignations in the wake of the Seaview Inquiry.
Board chairman Justice William Fischer says the 1994 Seaview air disaster occurred nine months before the board took office.
Justice Fischer says Transport Minister John Sharp has been trying to convince board members to stand down since the Coalition came to power on March 2nd.

He says Mr Sharp has indicated that resignations are necessary so the Transport Minister could meet what he called "his obligations". Justice Fischer says these obligations are jobs for the boys, in particular businessman and aviator, Dick Smith.
IR WARNING FOR FEDERAL GOVT
The Federal Government is being warned to accept Democrat amendments to its industrial relations reforms, or face the consequences.

National President of the Mining Union, John Maitland, says acceptance of the amendments is the logical outcome from everyone's point of view, unless the Government wants to force a double dissolution.
Mr Maitland says full-scale confrontation may result if the amendments aren't taken on board.
The Government's unlikely to get its Workplace Relations Bill through the Senate without the support of the Democrats, which is contingent on acceptance of the amendments.
COMPENSATION FOR MURRAY PROPERTIES
The Murray Darling Basin Commission has established guide lines for compensation to flooded property owners along the Murray River downstream of lake Hume.

Commission chairman, Professor John Lovering, says the commission will meet costs for damages in New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia which are specifically attributed to the additional releases of water from Lake Hume if legal liability is established.
He says the commission will provide short term financial assistance through emergency services for stock feed and assistance with moving stranded stock.
HOWARD PUSHES ASIA TIES
Prime Minister John Howard says Australia can develop its relationship with the United States and Asia without sacrificing its independence.
He's signalled that the relationship with the US and that country's commitment to the region will be key points of discussion when US President Bill Clinton visits Australia next month.

Speaking in Sydney last night, Mr Howard said Washington had confirmed its position as a leader in the region, by its recent joint declaration of security with Japan, the reaffirmation of ANZUS in Sydney, and a continuing commitment to APEC. He said no region will be more important to world prosperity and stability in the 21st Century than the Asia-Pacific region.
LUCKY ESCAPE AFTER CLIFF PLUNGE
Seven people, five of them children, were lucky to escape serious injury when their vehicle left the road near Toogoolawah, north-west of Brisbane, last night.
Police say the vehicle drove over a small cliff, before lodging in a tree.
Two rescue helicopters were among the emergency services that attended the scene.
HOWARD STANDS BY SHORT
Prime Minister John Howard is standing by his man this morning, despite admitting he considered sacking Assistant Treasurer, Jim Short.
Senator Short, who's responsible for banking, broke Mr Howard's ministerial guidelines by owning more than six thousand shares in the ANZ bank.
The guidelines compel Ministers to sell any shares they own in any company involved in their portfolio area.
However, Mr Howard says he believes Senator Short has behaved with propriety.
Senator Short says he regrets putting Mr Howard in a difficult position, because he says the Prime Minister is a man of the highest integrity.
He says he'll sell the shares, and donate the proceeds to charity.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
